projects.name: Specialty Account Type Reconciliation
projects.volume: ~42,000-row SF export reviewed; 1,089 specialty accounts corrected; 152 net-new accounts identified and added
projects.cause: Account Type and Sub-Type fields blank or incorrect post-Salesforce migration. No validation enforced at record creation, so RV, Marine, Equipment, Power Sports, and Commercial accounts were lumped under wrong types or missing type entirely. Required manual keyword filtering, false-positive review, and brand-matching across five category tabs.
projects.consequence: Account type drives territory reporting, sales segmentation, OEM program filtering, and the customer cube. Every specialty account with a bad type corrupted any report or KPI built on top of it — including MRR by segment, OEM program eligibility, and any specialty-segment performance tracking.

projects.name: Account Type = Dealership Bulk Update
projects.volume: 25,726 Account records updated to Type=Dealership via Python/Selenium automation; 69 records required manual intervention due to validation errors; project complete
projects.cause: Account Type field missing or unset for the dealership segment post-migration. No automated enforcement at entry means records accumulated in an undefined state, blocking any type-based filtering or reporting on the core customer segment.
projects.consequence: Dealership accounts are the primary customer universe. Blank type data means segment-level reporting, renewal forecasting, and OEM filtering on the dealership base all return unreliable results. Cascades to the customer cube and revenue guidance model.

projects.name: Contract Term & Renewal Term Backfill
projects.volume: 732 priority rows reviewed (active Sales AI assets with blank Contract Term and populated Lifecycle End Date); 300 filled with no conflicts, 15 conflicts flagged against Sage data, 415 deferred to Spence's Data Loader upload
projects.cause: Contract Term field blank for active assets — not carried over during Salesforce migration. Sage Intacct billing records contain the data but it was not mapped or backfilled, leaving a gap between what billing knows and what SF shows. Some records resolving via Sage report; others require manual PDF contract lookup.
projects.consequence: Contract Term feeds renewal forecasting, churn risk identification, and lifecycle management. Without it, Impel cannot accurately predict when contracts roll off or flag at-risk renewals — directly undermining the retention-focused GRR/NRR tracking Elizabeth and Andy prioritize.

projects.name: Asset Rooftop Field Backfill
projects.volume: 51 asset records reviewed; Rooftop field populated on the majority; flagged group-level accounts, one auction, and one ambiguous entry for Elizabeth to handle separately
projects.cause: Rooftop field blank on a subset of assets post-migration. When assets lack a rooftop, Elizabeth's customer cube report cannot pull the account ID, breaking downstream field population for the entire record.
projects.consequence: Without a rooftop, assets surface in Elizabeth's reporting with missing account data, corrupting MRR segmentation and any account-level analysis built on top of the customer cube. Fix enables Elizabeth to rerun reporting and auto-populate the remaining blank fields via the rooftop waterfall.

projects.name: Ourisman Rooftop Parent Account Alignment
projects.volume: 21 rooftops across 3 PODs (Pod 1: Robert Ourisman Jr., Pod 2: Christopher J. Ourisman, Pod 3: Danny Korengold); 3 accounts flagged as not found in SF (Lotus of Washington DC, Ourisman Tri-State Ford, Ourisman Tri-State Subaru); 1 structural discrepancy flagged (Ford Alexandria listed as one row on the sheet but exists as two separate SF accounts)
projects.cause: Parent Account field on rooftop-level accounts pointed directly to the top-level Ourisman Automotive Group instead of the correct POD-level intermediary account, or was left blank post-migration. The three-tier hierarchy (Rooftop > POD > Ourisman Automotive Group) was collapsed to two tiers for affected records.
projects.consequence: Without the correct POD-level parent, account hierarchy reporting breaks and any segmentation or rollup filtering built on the POD structure returns incorrect results. Ultimate Parent Account auto-populates correctly only once the POD intermediary is set, so dirty parent data cascades up through the entire Ourisman group hierarchy in SF.

projects.name: Account Type Field Bulk Update (Rooftop + Parent)
projects.volume: ~5,965 blank rooftop accounts set to Type=Dealership; 37 Parent accounts manually reviewed and categorized as Dealership, Dealership Group, or flagged as outliers; 12 ambiguous non-dealership accounts (Vital Software, Kawasaki Australia, Green RV, etc.) isolated in a separate tab for Luke to resolve
projects.cause: Account Type field blank on ~6,000 rooftop and parent-level records not captured by the prior bulk script run -- primarily international accounts (Australia, UK, Canada, Mexico, Middle East) outside the original domestic scope, plus parent-level accounts requiring judgment calls on entity type.
projects.consequence: Blank Type fields on rooftop accounts break segment-level reporting, OEM filtering, and any revenue analysis built on account type. Parent accounts miscategorized as generic "Parent" rather than Dealership Group corrupt hierarchy rollups and territory reporting across all child accounts.

projects.name: Billing Address Hygiene — Dealership Account Backfill
projects.volume: 2,281 filtered dealership accounts reviewed (from 5,235 total missing Billing Street); 378 verified addresses found at High or Medium confidence via Claude-assisted batch research; 844 additional accounts flagged across four categories: non-dealerships miscategorized as Dealership type (~208), international accounts with Billing Country incorrectly set to United States (~604 — Canadian, UK, Irish, Brazilian, Australian, and other foreign dealerships), test/placeholder records (39), and confirmed dead or closed accounts (21)
projects.cause: Billing Street field blank across 5,235 accounts post-migration. Majority owned by Data Migration user with no address data attached at import. Active rep-owned dealership accounts also affected, meaning billing records lacked physical location data for a significant portion of the active customer base. Underlying issues compounded by non-dealership entities and international accounts miscategorized as Dealership type with incorrect country fields.
projects.consequence: Missing billing addresses create gaps in invoice delivery accuracy and downstream billing system integrity. Wrong country fields on hundreds of international accounts (Canadian, Australian, Brazilian, Irish, and UK dealerships all marked as United States) risk misdirected billing and corrupt geographic segmentation in reporting. Non-dealerships and test records inflating the Dealership segment undermine any count-based reporting or quota modeling built on account type.

projects.name: Billing State Backfill — Asset Account Records
projects.volume: 103 US accounts with blank Billing State reviewed from Elizabeth's filtered asset report; 30 high-confidence records resolved in initial pass; second pass via Google Places API on 75 remaining rooftops returned 71 matches; 58 verified US states staged for Data Loader upload after removing 13 invalid/international results (Mexico, Canada, Brazil, Germany, Estonia, Italy, Saipan); file handed to Luke for import. Remaining accounts excluded: international entities with no applicable US state.
projects.cause: Billing State field blank on asset-linked account records. Missing address data at migration — accounts imported without geographic fields populated, leaving state blank across a subset of the active account base.
projects.consequence: Missing billing state breaks US territory assignment and geographic segmentation for affected accounts. Blank state on records tied to Elizabeth's customer cube causes those accounts to surface without location context, corrupting any region-based MRR or performance analysis.

projects.name: Billing Address Backfill — Google Places API Automation
projects.volume: 4,434 accounts in SF missing Billing Street; 1,347 excluded pre-API (409 non-US, 938 non-Rooftop); 3,087 Rooftop US accounts processed across 3 API runs; 1,775 verified addresses confirmed and staged for SF import; 651 accounts flagged to Needs Review (large dealer groups or ambiguous multi-location matches); 661 accounts returned no usable result
projects.cause: Billing Street field blank across thousands of rooftop accounts post-migration. Data Migration user import carried no physical address data. Manual research (proj-007) addressed a subset; remaining volume required automation to be viable at scale.
projects.consequence: Missing billing addresses break invoice delivery accuracy and downstream billing system integrity. Automating the lookup via Google Places API with phone-number anchoring, website domain matching, and rooftop count signals recovered 1,775 addresses in a single session — establishing a repeatable method for future address hygiene passes. Also surfaced ~938 non-Rooftop accounts miscategorized as Rooftop in SF, inflating the rooftop count and flagged as a separate cleanup item for Luke.

projects.name: Purchase Date Recovery Investigation — Legacy Asset Migration Gap
projects.volume: ~10,000 asset records with blank Purchase Date reviewed (4,793 of which are Active, not Cancelled); traced individual records (Anthem Chevrolet, Carter Myers Automotive) through Subscription → Contract → Opportunity chain per Stephen Wood's documented method; attempted bulk Salesforce report cross-reference against full blank population to estimate recoverable volume
projects.cause: Pre-CPQ-migration assets retain only a Renewal Opportunity link post-migration — the original Opportunity does not survive the Outsell-to-CPQ transition, so no purchase date exists to recover for those records. Confirmed at the individual-record level via manual trace and at the bulk level: account and product naming conventions don't reconcile cleanly between legacy Outsell and current CPQ systems, making automated matching unreliable across the full population.
projects.consequence: Structural data gap from the 2024 CPQ migration affecting revenue/reporting completeness on a meaningful share of active assets — not a data-entry oversight, and not resolvable through standard bulk remediation. Findings documented and delivered to Luke for leadership; recommendation is to treat this as closed rather than pursue bulk recovery, given the cost-to-confidence ratio of manual tracing. One-off accounts can still be traced case by case if a contractual or legal need arises.

projects.name: AIVA MRR / Net Unit Price Discrepancy — Pending Order Products Audit
projects.volume: 209 pending AIVA order products reviewed (Onboarding Status = Pending) via custom Order Products report; none fell below the $1k threshold on Net Unit Price or MRR; 23 records identified with a consistent $200/month gap between Net Unit Price ($1,000) and MRR ($1,200)
projects.cause: Traced one flagged record (Tri-City Chrysler Dodge Jeep Ram) to its full Order Product detail. MRR calculated off List/Unit Price (gross, pre-discount), while Net Unit Price correctly reflected the post-discount amount. No 'Net MRR' field exists on the Order Product object, so any discounted AIVA deal showed this same gap by design, not as a data entry error.
projects.consequence: Any reporting or forecasting built on MRR was using gross revenue, not actual net recurring revenue, on discounted accounts. Confirmed with Luke; both Net Unit Price and MRR set to 1,000 to match the existing correct value across all 23 records, staged with Order Product IDs and handed off for Data Loader upload.

projects.name: Service AI 1.0/2.0 Overlap Cleanup
projects.volume: 1,627 active Service AI 1.0/2.0 asset rows audited via Salesforce report; grouped by Account and Rooftop to isolate true overlaps from normal multi-rooftop accounts running different product versions; 4 rooftops identified with both products active simultaneously (Annapolis Nissan, Jim Hudson Toyota Sumter, Healey Brothers Cadillac, Riverside Nissan); new Lifecycle End Date calculated as one day prior to each account's Service AI 2.0 start date; staged with Asset IDs and handed to Luke for Data Loader upload after discovering Lifecycle End Date is a Data Loader-only field (no manual edit path; the field visible on the record page is a separate read-only formula field with the same label)
projects.cause: No automation existed to deactivate Service AI 1.0 assets upon Service AI 2.0 onboarding for legacy accounts, leaving both products active simultaneously. Riverside Nissan's overlap had gone undetected long enough that its corrected end date lands in the past, flagged separately to Luke for review before load.
projects.consequence: Overlapping active assets distort MRR and billing accuracy for the affected accounts and obscure true product adoption state. Fix also surfaced a page layout gap (the writable Lifecycle End Date field isn't exposed anywhere in the standard UI), worth flagging for a layout fix so this doesn't recur as a blocker on future cleanup work.

projects.name: AIVA Order Product Net Unit Price Restatement
projects.volume: 205 AIVA backlog Order Product records restated from Net Unit Price $1,200 to $1,000 per renegotiated rate; filtered report built with Luke on Order Products, exported to CSV, updated via Data Loader.io mapped on Order Product ID
projects.cause: Austin Beckner negotiated a new AIVA rate ($1,200 to $1,000) but the backlog of existing Order Product records still reflected the old rate. Luke walked through the correct field to update in person: Net Unit Price only, not the Quote Line Item MRR or Gross Activation MRR fields initially flagged, since those roll up from Net Unit Price and the converted currency field is a runtime formula that can't be mapped in Data Loader.
projects.consequence: Unrestated records would continue billing/reporting at the old rate despite the renegotiated terms, understating the rate change across the full AIVA backlog. Correction via Data Loader on Order Product ID keeps MRR (converted) and Net Unit Price aligned at the new rate going forward.

projects.name: Active Assets on Inactive Accounts
projects.volume: 2,320 active assets flagged on rooftop accounts not showing Active status, via Accounts with Assets - Custom report built with Luke at the rooftop level (not OEM level). Broken down as 2,152 Prospect, 100 Implementation, 68 Cancelled.
projects.cause: Asset Status and Account Status are not automatically kept in sync, active assets can persist on accounts that have moved to Prospect, Implementation, or Cancelled at the rooftop level with no automated flag or reconciliation step.
projects.consequence: Active assets tied to Cancelled accounts represent live billing/service exposure on terminated relationships. All 68 Cancelled-account assets were resolved directly. Report set to weekly Friday delivery to catch new instances going forward.

projects.name: Bundle Mixed-Completion States
projects.volume: Identified bundles where some component Order Products show Onboarding Status = Complete while others remain Pending, built via Excel-based conflict detection pipeline (COUNTIFS per unique Order Number) with color-coded output by rooftop.
projects.cause: Assets and billing for a bundle only trigger once every component Order Product in the bundle reaches Complete status; partial completion silently blocks the bundle from ever generating an asset with no visible flag in Salesforce report builder, which can't natively isolate mixed-status groups.
projects.consequence: Bundles stuck in partial completion delay both asset creation and billing indefinitely with no native alert. Pipeline delivered to Andy Bohlin to identify and unblock affected bundles.

projects.name: Account Relationship Deduplication — Phase 1 & 2
projects.volume: Phase 1: 67,079-row Account Relationship export reviewed with Katherine Brady; 6,838 records kept, 1,300 flagged for deletion, 9 flagged for review. Phase 2: active/implementation rooftop accounts with Sync to IDP = False reviewed against Luke's retention rules; 723 rows flagged for brand corrections plus 26 OEM mismatch records isolated for Luke's review. Both phases handed off.
projects.cause: Duplicate Account Relationship records and misaligned Related Brand/OEM fields accumulated with no dedup or validation pass since migration, driven by inconsistent MSA Pricing values, blank OEM fields resolved only by sibling-record inference, and no enforced rule preventing duplicate Account+OEM pairs from being created.
projects.consequence: Duplicate and misaligned relationship records inflate rooftop counts, distort OEM-level segmentation, and corrupt any account hierarchy or brand-based reporting built on Account Relationship data. Clean-up restores accuracy to relationship-based rollups; 26 OEM mismatches and Data Loader execution still pending Luke's confirmation.

projects.name: Toma Competitor Outreach List
projects.volume: 274 former Toma competitor rooftops reviewed with Katherine Brady; Salesforce data (Account ID, Status, Active/Inactive Assets, Pending Order Products, MRR) populated across columns L-Q in shared Google Sheet; Active Assets Names column added for upsell context; follow-up pass matched 3 additional pending/implementation accounts (Ferrari of Long Island, Fayetteville Dodge Ram, Rhythm CDJR). Delivered to Danny Rastegar for outreach.
projects.cause: No existing view combined competitor-displaced accounts with current Salesforce status, active product footprint, and pending orders, so sales had no way to prioritize or contextualize outreach to former Toma clients without manual account-by-account lookup.
projects.consequence: Sales now has a single reference sheet showing account status, live assets, and pending orders across all 274 rooftops, enabling targeted upsell/cross-sell outreach instead of blind competitor conquest contact.

projects.name: Order Product Asset Creation Gap
projects.volume: 3,328-row Order Product export reviewed (Onboarding Status = Complete, bundle children excluded); filtered out $0 total price and 1-month trial/promotional records; 1,399 records across 790 unique accounts confirmed as Complete with no corresponding asset created. Manual sampling of 10 records identified two failure sub-patterns. Documented in Obsidian and flagged to Salman for debugging.
projects.cause: Asset creation automation does not reliably trigger on Onboarding Status transitioning to Complete. Sampling showed both clean records with well-documented Pending-to-Complete transitions and no asset (trigger failure), and records with no logged status-change event or mismatched Onboarding Process fields (possible integrity or bypass issue).
projects.consequence: 790 accounts have completed onboarding with no corresponding asset, meaning no billing, no MRR attribution, and no product-adoption visibility for real, live implementations. Treated as a broken automation trigger rather than a leadership decision, so it sits outside the Pre-Decision Impact Mapping thesis as a sibling structural finding; Salman is debugging the root cause.

projects.name: Gumloop Canceled-Account Alert Agent
projects.volume: Built and validated with Benjy via SOQL workaround (Salesforce report UI editing blocked by org security policy). Filters: Account Status = Permanently Closed or Cancelled, Onboarding Status = Complete as active proxy, Order Product End Date excluded only if in the past. Returned 11 unique accounts and 66 active order products, matching prior week's manual count.
projects.cause: No automated alert existed to flag active, billable order products still sitting on canceled or permanently closed accounts, leaving this exposure discoverable only through ad hoc manual pulls.
projects.consequence: Validated build gives Sales Ops a repeatable, scheduled check for live billing/service exposure on terminated accounts. Also surfaced a secondary data gap: all 11 accounts returned as Cancelled with zero Permanently Closed matches, flagged to Benjy. Presented at the 7/21 scoping session to define the next 1-2 Gumloop automation targets.

projects.name: Sales Segment Override Audit
projects.volume: Gumloop SOQL pull on Sales_Segment_Override__c = true returned 20 accounts; 19 belong to two dealer groups (Gerald Jones: 8, Steet Ponte: 10), plus CDK Global as a standalone. Finding shared with Luke to confirm whether segment classifications are still accurate.
projects.cause: The override flag unlocks manual editing of the Sales Segment field rather than flagging an anomaly, so accounts can retain a manually-set segment indefinitely without revalidation against current account state.
projects.consequence: Concentration in two dealer groups raises the question of whether their segment classification still reflects reality or is stale from a past manual override. Awaiting Luke's read on whether this becomes a formal reclassification pass.

projects.name: Implementation Accounts With No Order Products
projects.volume: Luke requested a list of Account Status = Implementation accounts (Record Type = Rooftop and Non-Dealership) carrying zero Order Products. Built subtractively: List A of 1,046 Implementation accounts anti-joined against List B of 51,267 unique account IDs with at least one Order Product. Result was zero gap accounts; every account in scope already had Order Product coverage. Finding reported back to Luke verbally.
projects.cause: The 'Accounts With Order Products - CUSTOM' report type is an inner join, so it structurally cannot surface accounts with zero related Order Products. Third confirmed instance of an inner-join report type blocking a 'show me what's missing' query, alongside the Order Product to Asset join gap.
projects.consequence: Negative finding: no data integrity issue exists in this population, which closes the question rather than opening a cleanup. The real takeaway is structural, not data-level. Answering absence questions currently requires two exports and a manual anti-join every time, which is a repeatable cost until a custom report type or cross filter approach is standardized.

projects.name: Active Assets Missing Active Date
projects.volume: Ad hoc request from Luke for active assets carrying a Lifecycle Start Date but no Active Date. Reopened the 7/16 report (118 records at the time), found it filtered only on Status = Active and Active Date = blank without enforcing Lifecycle Start Date populated. Added the missing filter, trimmed columns to Asset Name, Account Name, Status, Lifecycle Start Date, Active Date. Final count 117.
projects.cause: Active Date is not enforced as a required field when an asset transitions to Active status, so assets can go live with a lifecycle start recorded but no active date, leaving the two lifecycle fields out of sync.
projects.consequence: Any tenure, time-to-activation, or lifecycle-duration calculation built on Active Date silently drops or misdates these 117 assets. Verifying the prior report's filters rather than resending the old number caught a genuine scope mismatch against what Luke actually asked for.

projects.name: Bundle Mixed-Completion States — July Rerun
projects.volume: Andy Bohlin requested a rerun of the 7/13 conflict report. No saved source export existed, so the Salesforce report was rebuilt from scratch on 'Order Products - Custom' and the conflict detection pipeline rerun. Result: 16 conflicting orders across 53 rows, 25 line items still Pending. Added a derived Brand column (Ford, GM, Honda, Kia, Lithia) at Andy's request, then a second pass adding MRR and NUP, quantifying $24,096.54 pending MRR and $26,274.50 pending NUP.
projects.cause: Same root cause as proj-015: bundles only generate assets and billing once every component Order Product reaches Complete, and Salesforce cannot natively isolate mixed-status groups. The rerun exposed a second-order problem, that no source export or saved report from the original run was retained, forcing a full rebuild.
projects.consequence: Roughly $24k in monthly recurring revenue is sitting unbilled behind partially-completed bundles with no native alert. Quantifying the dollar exposure rather than just the record count changed how the finding lands with a stakeholder. Standing lesson: save the Salesforce report object, not just the export, or every rerun is a rebuild.

projects.name: 360 WalkArounds Feature Gap Reports
projects.volume: Three gap reports requested by Austin Beckner and Kyle Greer via Art: Lithia dealers with 360 WalkArounds but no Feature Tour Merchandising (94 accounts), Lithia with 360 but no AI Virtual Booth (165 accounts), and all SMB dealers (Acquisition + Expansion) with 360 but no Feature Tour. First pass delivered as CSVs built through a pandas pivot/flag approach; Kyle then asked for native Salesforce reports, prompting a full rebuild using Cross Filters (Accounts WITH Assets / Accounts WITHOUT Assets). All three saved and links shared in a Slack group with Austin, Kyle, and Luke.
projects.cause: Salesforce cannot perform 'has asset A but not asset B' logic in a standard single-pass report; Cross Filters are the correct native mechanism and were not being used. Field discovery also surfaced that Lithia is not a Sales Segment value at all, it is a parent-child account structure, so the correct filter is Parent Account Name contains Lithia. Two Feature Tour asset name variants exist in the data, which a naive exact match would have missed.
projects.consequence: Cross-sell targets for the 360 install base are now standing, self-refreshing Salesforce reports rather than one-time CSVs that go stale the day they are sent. A near-miss was caught in review: report 3 had been duplicated from the Virtual Booth version and still carried the wrong cross filter.

projects.name: Assets Without Rooftop Assignment
projects.volume: Luke relayed a request from Johnathan Spence testing the hypothesis that some Order Products without assets had slipped through without a rooftop assignment. Built 'Assets Without Rooftop - Custom' on the Accounts with Assets report type with a null filter on Rooftop, trimmed to relevant columns. Returned 22 records. Report link and count sent back to Luke; Spence confirmed the result matched expectations.
projects.cause: Rooftop is not enforced on asset creation, but the 22 records are almost entirely legacy Cancelled or Inactive assets with zero Active records, meaning this is residue from historical data rather than an active automation failure.
projects.consequence: Hypothesis disproven. Explicitly ruled out as supporting evidence for the Salman asset creation gap escalation, which matters because attaching an unrelated 22-record population to a 1,399-record automation failure would have weakened the escalation rather than strengthened it.

projects.name: MRR Production by Rep and Month Matrix
projects.volume: Art requested a matrix report of MRR production by rep and month, US billing only, current fiscal year. First build on 'Order Products - Custom' grouped by Account Owner failed the requirement because no Team field exists on Order Products or on 'Accounts With Order Products - CUSTOM'. Rebuilt from Austin Beckner's existing YTD Bookings by Rep Sales Scorecard on 'Opportunities with Quotes and Quote Lines', which already carries Sales Team logic, with Sales Team as the outer row group, Opportunity Owner nested, and Close Date by calendar month as columns.
projects.cause: Sales team structure is not modeled on the Order Product or Account objects, so team-level revenue reporting is only possible on the Opportunity side. Luke confirmed a role hierarchy build in Sandbox is the real long-term fix.
projects.consequence: Team-level production reporting works today only by inheriting logic from one pre-existing scorecard report, which is a single point of failure. Checking whether an existing report already solves the join is faster than building the schema from scratch.

projects.name: SET Toyota Dealer Product Coverage Matrix
projects.volume: Austin requested active-asset coverage by product category for Art across 43 SET Toyota dealers in SET_Service_AI_Dealers.xlsx. Pulled a Salesforce export on Accounts with Assets (Account Name, Asset Name, Product Family, Status), re-pulled after finding Digital Asset Status entirely blank and the correct field being asset-level Status. Delivered 8 binary coverage columns: Chat AI, Sales AI, Service AI, AI Marketing, Ad Tech, Merchandising Hardware, Merchandising Software, Setup.
projects.cause: Dealer names in the source file did not match Salesforce account names because of typos, dropped suffixes, and abbreviations, requiring fuzzy matching plus one manual Salesforce lookup to resolve Village Toyota to Village Toyota Homosassa. AI Communications is also a single Product Family covering distinct sellable products, so sub-categorization had to be done by asset name keyword rather than by the schema.
projects.consequence: Head of sales now has a whitespace view of product coverage across the SET Toyota book. The deeper issue is that Product Family does not map cleanly to how the products are actually sold, so any product-level analysis requires manual bucketing by asset name.

projects.name: Internal vs Cancelled Churn Reclassification Backfill
projects.volume: Board-level data correction with Andy Bohlin and Cecilia: identify churn records coded Internal that should have been Cancelled, and backfill a 'When should it have been cancelled?' date column. 1,061 rows deduplicated to 239 distinct Cancellation Reason Details strings, dates inferred and filled for 142 cases, 38 ambiguous cases returned grouped by failure type (vague relative time, year or quarter only, disputed dates, conflicting dates, implied but unstated). Phase 1 delivered to the Andy/Cecilia/Luke group.
projects.cause: Cancel dates were never captured as structured data. The only record of when an account should have been cancelled lives in free-text retention case notes, so recovering the date requires parsing prose rather than querying a field. Cecilia also writes 'should have fallen off' language in the Notes field, not only in Description, so the first pass missed a source column entirely until Andy added a vlookup at column AJ.
projects.consequence: Miscoded Internal churn understates true cancellation volume in board reporting. 142 of 239 distinct cases recovered on the first pass; second pass pending against the newly populated Notes column plus whatever Cecilia resolves manually. Structural point: this is a field-capture failure, not a data entry failure, and it will recur until a cancel date is required at case close.

deliverables.name: Legacy Outsell Purchase Date Recovery — Findings Memo
deliverables.audience: Luke, for leadership (Devin/Wayne/Andy if it comes up)
deliverables.summary: Purchase dates for ~10,000 legacy Outsell-migrated assets cannot be recovered at scale. The Renewal Opportunity link is the only thing that survives the migration on most records, and there is no remaining path back to the original purchase date. Manual tracing works per-account but costs ~25 clicks across 4 records for an estimate, not a confirmed date — not worth it across the full population.
deliverables.context: Built from Stephen Wood's walkthrough in the 6/23 Sales Ops standup, after Luke asked the team to document findings and prepare to present them up the chain rather than keep digging. Delivered as a one-page BLUF memo (Word doc) so leadership can skim the conclusion and stop, or read the supporting detail if they want it. In other words: I wrote a memo that the C suite will possibly see.... that's pretty cool.
